thread:
Liz (AE): Heads-up — Aurora Finance asked for a custom instruct variant of rex-7b with 64k context and aggressive quant (int4). They want preview in 2 weeks. Priority?
Maya (ML Eng): two quick Qs — do they need instruction-tuned behavior or just a wrapper prompt? and is data residency a hard requirement?
Liz (AE): instruction-tuned. They have PHI-like docs, so private deployment preferred but initial eval can be hosted w/ token redaction.
Samir (ML Ops): ok. big asks: long context + int4. Both increase risk of quality regressions. Need checklist: unit evals, regression tests vs hosted baseline, perf numbers, memory profile, safety scans.
Maya (ML Eng): agreed. I'll run a small quant sweep (awq + gptq) and a long-context consistency eval using their 64k doc prompt set. Quick notes: int4 lowers memory ~2.8x but increases non-deterministic token occasionally.
Maya (ML Eng): trying quant locally now. snippet:```bash
./quantize --model rex-7b.pt --out rex-7b-awq-4bit.bin --method awq --block-size 128
```
Maya (ML Eng): initial run: GPU mem peak 23.6GB -> 8.5GB after quant, batch=1 latency (first token) 220ms hosted sim, steady-state per-token 6ms (on A100).
Jon (SRE): routing note — longctx will need KV cache changes. Canary on dedicated pool only; prefer not to mix with non-64k traffic. Also need autoscale buffer + fallback to rex-7b-16k if memory spikes.
Samir (ML Ops): test matrix I propose: [base 7b fp16, base int8, awq int4, gptq int4], each with instruct-tuning (LoRA) applied. Run: 1) perplexity on holdout, 2) exact-match on QAs, 3) semantic similarity regression vs hosted baseline.
Maya (ML Eng): I ran a quick QA regression on our finance devset: fp16 baseline EM=72.3%, awq-int4 EM=70.1% (-2.2pts), gptq-int4 EM=68.9% (-3.4pts). Rouge-L similar trend. Will run more seeds.
Liz (AE): Aurora tolerance is +/-3% on key metrics. So awq-int4 might be OK, gptq-int4 borderline.
Samir (ML Ops): safety & hallucination checks: run our hallucination harness and PII detector on 2k prompts. Also verify deterministic KV caching across restarts.
Maya (ML Eng): flag: instruction-tuning LoRA seems to amplify some output style drift under int4. Need targeted eval prompts (policy/legal templates) from Aurora to validate. Liz can collect?
Liz (AE): I'll get the sample templates today.
Jon (SRE): infra checklist: 1) allocate 2x gpu nodes (48GB) for canary, 2) enable trace-level logging for first 1k requests, 3) automatic rollback trigger if 5xx > 0.5% or p95 token latency > 400ms.
Samir (ML Ops): rollout plan: dev -> dedicated canary (Aurora tenant) -> 10% production traffic -> 50% -> full. Each stage gated by quality regression dashboard (EM, rouge, hallucinations).
Maya (ML Eng): quick perf note: with awq-int4 + prefix caching we can keep p95 gen latency ~350ms for 4k prompts, but 64k prompts push to ~1.1s p95 unless we stream chuncks and prewarm KV.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: "Created canary cluster: canary-aurora-rex7b-64k (2 nodes)" :rocket:
Samir (ML Ops): next steps I assign: Maya -> quant sweep & eval artifacts (due in 4 days). Jon -> provision canary infra + SLO hooks (due EOD tomorrow). Liz -> collect Aurora templates + confirm private vs hosted plan (due 48h).
Maya (ML Eng): noted. I'll attach eval CSVs + short notebook when done.
Liz (AE): thanks team. Aurora wants a short demo after canary — tentatively schedule w/ them for two weeks from now.
Samir (ML Ops): one last thing — include fallback routing rule: if int4 model fails more than X regression checks, route to fp16 hosted variant with auto-throttle.
Maya (ML Eng): put that rule in the rollout playbook. I'll add the exact thresholds once I finish the eval. :+1:
Liz (AE): perfect. cc @Aurora-prod-contact when we have demo date.
Jon (SRE): I'll post the infra PR link once provisioned.
Maya (ML Eng): uploading first quant logs now.
